decisions.reason: Presented on its own page and tied to the firm's core drain-housing technology, it reflects visible investment and commitment that management would not write off after one year.

Floor-level shower drainage is central to the firm's announced direction toward low-profile, accessible systems, so dropping it would contradict its strategy even though it is only mentioned on the website.
A designer drainage product with its own page embodies the firm's design-quality positioning, and any early weakness can still be attributed to the market ramp-up.
Public commitment is modest, but the integrated-slope shower element fits the move toward integrated low-profile systems, so management would give it more time.
The firm publicly claimed to have developed this backflow-protected drain itself, so the investment and visible commitment make keeping it highly likely.
Only mentioned on the website and peripheral to the firm's direction, it is the easiest product to drop, but one year is too short for its results to rule out temporary causes.
